text:
maya: heads up — acme-prod is hitting 503s for the past 30m. Customer reports requests failing almost immediately and retries piling up. stack traces attached from their request header

maya: sample client error:
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 15:12:01 GMT
x-request-id: r-7f4a2b
error: upstream inference worker crashed (SIGSEGV)
trace: connection reset by peer
```

maya: server-side snippet from our logs (host id i-0a1b2c3d):
```
[2026-03-17T15:11:59Z] runtime: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 42 [running]:
  github.com/redwood/infer/serving.(*tokenizer).Tokenize+0x1f3
  /workspace/infer/tokenizer.go:128
SIGSEGV: segmentation fault
```

dan_oncall: oncall taking this. Can you paste the full host/container id and recent deploy tag? Did this start after the last quant swap?

maya: host i-0a1b2c3d, container c-9d8f7e, deploy tag: release/2026-03-16-quant-swap. Impacting ~12% of requests to model:redwood-bert-quant-v2. Customer says it started after a sudden increase in short chat QPS.

leo_runtime: logging — looks like tokenizer nil deref in the C binding path after fastpath swap. Also seeing repeated OOM messages before the crash in dmesg for the same container: 
```
Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (infer-runner) total-vm: 12G, anon-rss: 9G
nvidia: Xid (PCIe) error, GPU=0
```

emily_sre: if it's OOM then container is being restarted by kube. Can we confirm whether the kernel OOM or the process itself segfaulted first? Need to know to narrow down fallback policy.

dan_oncall: grabbing metrics now — memory ramp precedes the segfault by ~3s in 6/8 repro samples. Repro steps from acme: they run a 3-token prompt at high QPS with batching disabled (customer uses per-request streaming). They provided a curl that reliably triggers within 2-3 attempts.

acme-cs: repro curl (redacted keys):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer ****" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"model":"redwood-bert-quant-v2","input":"hi","stream":true,"max_tokens":3}'
```

leo_runtime: thanks — I can reproduce locally on a small cluster when I disable batching and force short sequences. Repro triggers either a GPU OOM or segmentation fault inside tokenizer C-API. Suspect race between KV prefetch and tokenizer state after quant swap.

maya: customer is asking for ETA and is concerned about billing — they see many retries and want credits for the failed requests.

emily_sre: mitigation plan:
- Immediately add routing rule to send redwood-bert-quant-v2 traffic to redwood-bert-quant-v1 (older variant) for acme-prod (canary) and enable automatic fallback to cpu-emulate for short inputs.
- Temporarily enable small-request batching to avoid prefetch hotpath.
- Increase pod memoryRequest limit on the worker pool by +2Gi for the next 2 hours while we triage.
- Collect core dumps + pstack + nvidia-smi output on next crash.

dan_oncall: executing step 1 now — routing rule applied to acme-prod. Also rolling a quick memory bump: kube patch on node pool. Will monitor 5m.

deploy-bot: routing change applied by dan_oncall at 2026-03-17T15:19:12Z — route(redwood-bert-quant-v2 -> redwood-bert-quant-v1) for service acme-prod

maya: customer confirms 15m later: errors dropped to near zero after the routing change. They still want root cause.

leo_runtime: next steps for RCA:
- Reproduce with fuzzer that toggles quant swap + disable-batching to try to trigger in CI.
- Add guard checks in tokenizer C binding to avoid nil accesses during swap.
- Add telemetry on prefetch/kv cache invalidation timing.
- Postmortem + customer credit proposal.

emily_sre: assign owners: leo_runtime for runtime fix, dan_oncall for deployment/band-aid, maya for customer comms and billing. We'll sync in the incident meeting at 16:00 UTC.

maya: noted. I'll draft the customer message and propose 10% credit for the failed window.

support-bot: incident created I-2026-0317-21: "upstream tokenizer nil-deref causing 503s for acme-prod" assigned to SRE and Runtime teams.

dan_oncall: monitoring graphs show memory spike mitigation holding. Will follow up with logs/core if it reoccurs. :thumbsup:
